Title:

Acute Inhalation Study with Sidestream Cigarette Smoke of Standard Reference
Cigarette 2R1 and Ammonia Vapor on Rats

SD: WRE

Experimental Part: 1984

Objective:

Determine the irritancy of sidestream smoke components

Cigarette Codes:

2R1 (SS), NH\( _{4} \)OH

Test Parameter:

Respiratory frequency,  \( CO_{2} \)  exhalation

\( ^{*} \)

-1.37

Study Design:

11 groups with 20 male Sprague Dawley rats, each; head-only exposed for 7 h/d to SS (13 to 253  \( \mu \) g/l TPM) and 32 to 410  \( \mu \) g/l NH \( _{4} \) OH

Results / Comments:

- In Rats, ammonia in SS seems to contribute not more than 10 % to the total irritancy of sidestream smoke.

- Based on Alarie's (1973) published results on the relative irritating potency of various chemicals, it is estimated that acrolein and formaldehyde contribute more than ammonia to the irritancy of SS.
